opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez is a full-time Payroll Specialist. He requests write access to Payroll, which he owns. Full-time employees may have up to write, and role ownership permits admin, so write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E046 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note says full_time, but I rely on the Security record). Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training. Basic training limits to read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: There is a conflict between the HR note (full_time) and the Security note (contractor with basic security training, relying on the Security record). Employee E046 requests write access to Payroll. Per policy, contractors may have write only with advanced security training; with basic training the maximum is read. Since the requested level (write) exceeds the maximum (read), I grant the maximum of read. Approval is never more than requested, so read is appropriate.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Requested: write.

If full_time: max is write (role owns system, so admin possible, but requested is write). Write is at or below max → grant write.

If contractor with basic training: max is read (write requires advanced training). Write is above max → grant read.
